propositions: The snapshot janitor's absolute free-space watermark (2 GiB) is disk-size-blind and unreachable on a 30-GiB root until 93.3% used, above the 85% alarm floor and the 90% peak actually reached.

Every review materializes a fresh ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree keyed on a tip advancing every ~26 seconds, generating ~4.4 GiB/h growth on the container writable layer because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset.
The janitor runs but cannot trigger before the alarm because its cold-trim is dead code (container lifetime < 7 days) and the byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 is not implemented in _gc_pass.
A volume-relative watermark term must replace the absolute floor so the trigger sits below the operator's alarm threshold on any volume size.
Reclamation with hysteresis must target a point above the trigger to prevent re-firing every interval instead of reaching a stable floor.
